<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Annotation Instructions</h2>

<div id="A1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">These instructions describe how to annotate <span id="A1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">LeakageBench</span> for privacy redaction. The goal is to mark <em id="A1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">every visible region</em> on a page that contains an in-scope identifier, using tight bounding boxes and an exact transcription of the text.</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.1 </span>What to label (schema)</h3>

<div id="A1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Annotate <span id="A1.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">all</span> instances of the following fine-grained PII types (must match exactly):</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="A1.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Direct identifiers:</span> <span id="A1.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Person Name, Address, Email Address, Phone Number</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Linkage keys:</span> <span id="A1.I1.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Customer ID, Employee ID, Policy Number, ID Card Number, File Number, Reference Number, Contract Number, Invoice Number, Cheque Number, Registration Number, Call Sign, DA Case Number</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Operational references:</span> <span id="A1.I1.i3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Agency Code, Agency Ref, Advertiser Ref</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Contextual identifiers:</span> <span id="A1.I1.i4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Date, Organization Name, Business ID, Location</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I1.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Other (visual PII):</span> <span id="A1.I1.i5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Signature</span> (handwritten signatures or signature marks)</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Important:</h4>

<div id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If a page contains multiple identifiers, annotate <em id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">all of them</em>. This benchmark is safety-driven: a page is considered leaked if <em id="A1.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">any</em> in-scope identifier is missed.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.2 </span>How to draw boxes (localization)</h3>

<div id="A1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="A1.I2" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A1.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Draw a <span id="A1.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">tight bounding box</span> around the <span id="A1.I2.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">visible identifier text</span> (or signature mark). Boxes should cover the characters with minimal background.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Do <span id="A1.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">not</span> box entire rows, table blocks, or paragraphs unless <em id="A1.I2.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">the entire region is PII</em>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If an identifier spans multiple lines (e.g., an address block), draw <span id="A1.I2.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">one box covering the full multi-line span</span> if the tool supports it. Otherwise, use multiple boxes and keep the transcription consistent across lines.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I2.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I2.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I2.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If the identifier is repeated on the page (e.g., header and footer), annotate <span id="A1.I2.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">each occurrence</span> separately.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.3 </span>How to enter the text value (transcription)</h3>

<div id="A1.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="A1.I3" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A1.I3.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I3.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I3.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Transcribe the <span id="A1.I3.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">value exactly as it appears</span> in the image.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I3.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I3.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I3.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Do <span id="A1.I3.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">not</span> correct spelling, punctuation, casing, or spacing.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I3.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I3.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I3.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Do <span id="A1.I3.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">not</span> normalize formats (dates, phone numbers, IDs, etc.). Keep the original formatting.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I3.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I3.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I3.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For multi-line values, use the literal token <span id="A1.I3.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">\n</span> to indicate line breaks (e.g., <span id="A1.I3.i4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Line1\nLine2\nLine3</span>).</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.4 </span>Type selection rules (common edge cases)</h3>

<div id="A1.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Use the most specific schema type that matches the <em id="A1.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">role</em> of the text on the page.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="A1.I4" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A1.I4.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I4.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I4.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I4.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Person Name:</span> Names of individuals (signers, recipients, customers, employees). If the page contains initials, titles, or suffixes as part of the displayed name, include them as shown.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I4.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I4.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I4.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I4.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Organization Name:</span> Company, agency, or institution names. Do not label generic department words unless they clearly function as an entity name in context.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I4.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I4.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I4.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I4.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Address:</span> Postal addresses (street + city/state/zip) or address blocks. Include apartment/suite/unit numbers if present.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I4.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I4.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I4.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I4.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Email Address:</span> Email addresses exactly as written.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I4.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I4.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I4.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I4.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Phone Number:</span> Telephone numbers (including extensions if shown).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I4.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I4.i6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I4.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I4.i6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Date:</span> Dates and date ranges as written (including billing periods and coverage periods).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I4.i7" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I4.i7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I4.i7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I4.i7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Invoice Number / Contract Number / Policy Number / Reference Number / File Number:</span> Choose the type based on the field label and context. If the page label says “Invoice #”, annotate as <span id="A1.I4.i7.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Invoice Number</span>. If it says “Policy No.”, annotate as <span id="A1.I4.i7.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Policy Number</span>, etc.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I4.i8" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I4.i8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I4.i8.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I4.i8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Customer ID / Employee ID / Business ID:</span> Use when the page explicitly indicates the identifier category (e.g., “Customer ID”, “Employee ID”, “UEN/ABN/VAT”, “Business ID”).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I4.i9" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I4.i9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I4.i9.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I4.i9.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Call Sign:</span> Broadcast or station identifiers (e.g., <span id="A1.I4.i9.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">KXAS</span>, <span id="A1.I4.i9.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">WLAX/WEUX</span>) when used as a station/call sign.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I4.i10" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I4.i10.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I4.i10.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I4.i10.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Agency Code / Agency Ref / Advertiser Ref / DA Case Number:</span> Use when the page contains explicit labeled codes corresponding to these identifiers.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I4.i11" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I4.i11.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I4.i11.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.I4.i11.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Signature:</span> Handwritten signature marks or signature scribbles. Do not label printed names near the signature line as <span id="A1.I4.i11.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Signature</span>;</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">When unsure.</h4>

<div id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If you cannot confidently map a span to one of the schema types, <span id="A1.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">do not guess</span>. Prefer leaving it unannotated over inventing a type.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.5 </span>Pre-marked / highlighted regions</h3>

<div id="A1.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Some pages may contain regions already highlighted or redacted (e.g., dark blocks, overlays, pre-annotations). These are <span id="A1.SS5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">not reliable ground-truth evidence of PII</span>.</p>
<ul id="A1.I5" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A1.I5.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I5.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I5.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Do <span id="A1.I5.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">not</span> annotate pre-redacted regions where the text is no longer readable.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I5.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I5.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I5.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If the text remains visible despite highlighting, annotate it normally based on what is visible.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.6 </span>Quality checklist before submitting a page</h3>

<div id="A1.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Before finalizing a page, quickly verify:</p>
<ul id="A1.I6" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A1.I6.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I6.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I6.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All visible names, emails, phone numbers, and addresses are boxed.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I6.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I6.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I6.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All visible linkage keys (invoice/contract/policy/reference/file/customer IDs, etc.) are boxed.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I6.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I6.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I6.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Boxes are tight and not overly large.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A1.I6.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A1.I6.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.I6.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Transcriptions are verbatim and include <span id="A1.I6.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">\n</span> for multi-line items.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Baseline Reproducibility Details</h2>

<div id="A2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This appendix records the implementation choices needed to reproduce the baseline evaluations.
No baseline is trained or tuned on LeakageBench.
All outputs are converted to the same format: PII type, optional value, confidence score, and image-space bounding box.</p>
</div>

</table>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 6: </span>Baseline inventory. “OCR / boxes” indicates the source of text and localization boxes. “Type scope” indicates whether the system uses built-in labels mapped to LeakageBench, a restricted PII label set, or the full benchmark schema.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Type scope controls which LeakageBench labels a system can emit before scoring; it is used only for schema coverage and supported-type leakage, not for full-schema evaluation.</p>
</div>
<section id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">OCR-dependent conversion.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">OCR-dependent systems detect PII over recognized text and recover page coordinates from OCR word boxes.
Presidio uses Tesseract OCR.
The stronger OCR-dependent baselines use Amazon Textract word boxes, except for services that provide their own text recognition or span interface.
For each detected text span, we align the span to OCR words and use the minimal enclosing rectangle over the matched word boxes.
Unaligned detections are discarded.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Schema mapping and unsupported types.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All predictions are mapped to the LeakageBench schema before scoring.
For systems with built-in or restricted taxonomies, unmapped prediction labels are discarded.
Under full-schema evaluation, unsupported gold types remain in scope and count as missed detections.
Supported-type leakage filters gold labels to the entity types each system can emit.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">OCR-free conversion and validation.</h4>

<div id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">OCR-free VLMs receive the page image directly and output normalized boxes, which we convert to pixel coordinates before scoring.
The full LeakageBench schema is supplied in the prompt, so OCR-free schema coverage is <math id="A2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.0</annotation></semantics></math> by configuration.
Malformed outputs, labels outside the schema, invalid boxes, and out-of-bounds boxes are scored as empty predictions; we do not apply model-specific repair or manual correction.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>

<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">

<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Schema Coverage</h2>

<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para">

under each baseline’s schema mapping or prompting interface. Coverage
indicates which LeakageBench types the evaluated configuration was
allowed to emit; it does not measure intrinsic model capability or
detection accuracy.</p>

<section id="A7" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix G </span>IoU Threshold Sweep</h2>

<div id="A7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A7.T10" title="Table 10 ‣ Appendix G IoU Threshold Sweep ‣ LeakageBench: Document-Level Leakage Risk for Redacting Personally Identifiable Information in Document Images" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a> reports a threshold sweep over the IoU matching criterion <math id="A7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau\in\{0.50,0.75,0.95\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0.50</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.75</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.95</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau\in\{0.50,0.75,0.95\}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Lowering <math id="A7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> relaxes box tightness requirements, while higher <math id="A7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> requires tighter spatial alignment.
Although entity-level F1 changes substantially with <math id="A7.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math>, document-level leakage remains high across thresholds.</p>
</div>

severity using the headline type-aware matcher.

OCR-dependent systems using type-agnostic matching at
IoU <math id="A9.T14.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau=0.75" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.75</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau=0.75</annotation></semantics></math>. The upper panel reports exclusive failure shares;
the lower panel gives their denominators and secondary diagnostic
counts. Value-unavailable instances remain in the leakage total but
are excluded from attribution percentages. OCR partial is a secondary
flag on OCR-miss instances. Dashes indicate unavailable vendor OCR.</figcaption>

      should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for
      all.</p>
